stubs.angle: What does a program print when an async method writes, awaits Task.CompletedTask, writes again and the caller writes before awaiting the returned task?
stubs.answerHinge: An async method runs synchronously on the caller's thread until it awaits an incomplete task, and awaiting an already completed task does not yield, so the output is 1243.

stubs.angle: What does a program print when an async Task method throws before any await, the caller prints A after the call and catches the exception around a later await, printing B?
stubs.answerHinge: An exception inside an async Task method is captured into the returned task instead of being thrown at the call site, and it surfaces only at await, so the output is AB.

stubs.angle: What does a program print when Task.WhenAll gets two TaskCompletionSource tasks that are completed in reverse order and the result array is joined?
stubs.answerHinge: Task.WhenAll returns results in the order of the input tasks, not in completion order, so the output is 1,2.

stubs.angle: What happens to the calling thread when an async method reaches await on an I/O task that has not completed yet?
stubs.answerHinge: The method suspends and returns an incomplete task to its caller, so the thread is released to do other work; await neither blocks the thread nor starts a new one.

stubs.angle: What does calling CancellationTokenSource.Cancel do to a task whose loop never checks the token it was given?
stubs.answerHinge: Cancellation is cooperative: Cancel only marks the token and runs registered callbacks, so code that never observes the token keeps running to completion.

stubs.angle: What exception type names does a program print when it calls Wait() and then GetAwaiter().GetResult() on a task faulted with TimeoutException, catching and printing each?
stubs.answerHinge: Task.Wait and Result wrap the failure in AggregateException, while GetAwaiter().GetResult() and await rethrow the original exception, so the output is AggregateException TimeoutException.

stubs.angle: What does a program print when it awaits Task.WhenAll over two faulted tasks and in the catch block prints the caught exception type and the count of the WhenAll task's InnerExceptions?
stubs.answerHinge: await on a WhenAll task rethrows only the first inner exception, while the task's Exception property still holds all of them, so the output is InvalidOperationException 2.

stubs.angle: What does a program print for the task status and a ran flag when Task.Run receives a token that was already cancelled before the call?
stubs.answerHinge: Task.Run checks the token before starting the delegate, so the delegate never runs and the task ends in the Canceled state, printing Canceled False.

stubs.angle: What does a program print when it awaits the result of Task.Factory.StartNew with an async lambda that waits on an uncompleted TaskCompletionSource and then prints whether the inner task is completed?
stubs.answerHinge: StartNew with an async lambda returns Task<Task> and the outer task completes as soon as the lambda returns its inner task, so the inner task is still incomplete and False is printed, unlike Task.Run, which unwraps.

stubs.angle: Find the line where a non-async method creates a resource in a using declaration and returns the resource's ReadAsync task directly, so the program fails with ObjectDisposedException.
stubs.answerHinge: Returning the task without awaiting it leaves the using scope immediately, so the resource is disposed before the asynchronous operation finishes; the fix is async plus return await.

stubs.angle: Find the line that makes a method accepting a CancellationToken finish with completed instead of canceled after the caller cancels, because the inner Task.Delay call is made without the token.
stubs.answerHinge: A token only cancels the calls it is passed to, so an inner await that does not receive the token keeps running and the method completes normally.

stubs.angle: Which of these ways of waiting for tasks block the calling thread: Task.Wait, Task.Result, GetAwaiter().GetResult(), Task.WaitAll, await, Task.WhenAll, Task.WhenAny?
stubs.answerHinge: Wait, Result, GetAwaiter().GetResult() and WaitAll block the current thread, which is what makes sync-over-async deadlocks possible, while await, WhenAll and WhenAny return tasks and do not block.

stubs.angle: What does a program print when an async method awaits a default TaskCompletionSource task and then writes C, while the caller calls SetResult and then writes B?
stubs.answerHinge: Without TaskCreationOptions.RunContinuationsAsynchronously, SetResult runs the awaiting continuation synchronously on the calling thread before returning, so the output is CB.

stubs.angle: How many times is Post called on a custom SynchronizationContext subclass whose Post delegates to the base implementation, after it is installed and the code awaits Task.Yield twice?
stubs.answerHinge: The first await captures the custom context and posts to it, but the base Post runs the continuation on a thread pool thread where SynchronizationContext.Current is null, so the second await captures nothing and the output is 1.

stubs.angle: What does the C# compiler generate for an async method, and when does that code allocate on the heap?
stubs.answerHinge: The method becomes a stub plus a state machine (a struct in Release builds) with hoisted locals, a state field and MoveNext driven by an async method builder, and the state machine is boxed to the heap only when an await first suspends.

stubs.angle: Why does a ValueTask backed by an IValueTaskSource carry a short token, and what does that token protect against?
stubs.answerHinge: The IValueTaskSource object is reset and reused for the next operation, and the token identifies which operation a ValueTask belongs to, so consuming a stale ValueTask can be detected instead of silently reading another operation's result.

stubs.angle: Which statements about CancellationTokenSource in .NET 10 are true, covering linked sources, disposal, CancelAfter and TryReset?
stubs.answerHinge: A linked source registers callbacks on its parent tokens and must be disposed to unregister them, and TryReset (since .NET 6) succeeds only when the source has not been cancelled, because a cancelled token can never return to the uncancelled state.

stubs.angle: Your team maintains a shared library and colleagues ask for both sync and async versions of every method; what policy do you set and why?
stubs.answerHinge: Expose async APIs only where the underlying work is truly asynchronous I/O, and ship neither Task.Run wrappers over sync code (async over sync) nor .Result wrappers over async code (sync over async), because the caller is the one who knows whether offloading or blocking is acceptable.

stubs.angle: A WPF team is converting its data layer to async and the UI calls it from 40 places through .Result, with freezes already reported; how do you plan the migration without stopping releases?
stubs.answerHinge: Migrate incrementally with async all the way up to the event handlers, keep the genuinely synchronous paths alongside instead of adding blocking wrappers, and enforce the rule with analyzers and review, because sync-over-async on the UI thread deadlocks.

stubs.angle: How do you design cancellation so that when a client abandons a request that fans out to several downstream services, all the work it started stops?
stubs.answerHinge: Derive one token per request from the client abort signal linked with a timeout budget and pass it through every async call and outgoing request, because cooperative cancellation stops only the work that receives and observes the token.
